newsitem.title: UK: UK financial services profits up sharply in Q4 - CBI.
newsitem.headline: UK financial services profits up sharply in Q4 - CBI.

text.p: Business confidence and profitability rose sharply in the UK financial services sector in the fourth quarter of 1996, a survey by the Confederation of British Industry showed.
Business optimism in financial services rose at the fastest rate since the first survey in December 1989 and rose for the fourth consecutive quarter.

"Strong growth in the financial services mirrors the pick-up in the overall economy with firms expecting further, but less pronounced, increases over the coming months," Sudhir Junankar, the CBI's associate director of economic analysis, said.
"Firms are increasing their profitability as business grows and by cutting jobs to control the rise in their costs."

The survey, conducted by the CBI and Coopers & Lybrand, showed the balance of firms reporting increased confidence stood at 61 percent, up from 46 percent in the third quarter and only four percent in the last quarter of 1995.
